source_refs.note: Unnumbered heading Encapsulation under 3.2, with its Tidbit, as printed (PDF 39, printed 35).

blocks.text: Encapsulation is a concept in Object Oriented Programming (OOP) where we bundle data (variables) and methods (functions) into a single unit (class) and restrict direct access to the data.
Unlike languages like Java or C++, Python does not have strict "private" or "protected" keywords. Instead, it relies on naming conventions to signal how data should be accessed.

blocks.title: Tidbit
blocks.text: Hide the data and control access using methods.
